opening: The record concerns a conservation workshop tracing a damaged artifact through several rooms. By the time investigators reconstructed the treatment that stabilized the artifact, casual impressions had produced several plausible candidates. The reviewers therefore used only the local rules stated in the surviving record.

scenes.prose: Before comparing names, the panel read the governing notes aloud. For this incident, the board declared the certified restoration lead protocol active; ordinary rank and reputation did not count. The panel fixed one shared status scale for the whole inquiry: dormant counted as 0; stable counted as 1; waking counted as 2; open counted as 3; latent counted as 4; clear counted as 5. The local tally began at 13. In order it used relation, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol statuses with coefficients 3, 13, 2, 7, 5, 11. At each stream, the panel squared the current tally, added that stream's coefficient times its status value, and kept the remainder modulo 97. It made three passes: first in the stated order, then in reverse order with the coefficients reversed, then once more in the stated order with the coefficient list rotated one place left. Without resetting the tally, it repeated that complete three-pass cycle 122 times.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 1

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. When the pairing sheet was recovered, Jules Meier's apprentice lineage stood at stable. Even the damaged roster still marked Logan Kline's apprentice lineage as dormant. A clock-backed entry listed Yael Patel's work interval as clear. The chemical response that followed Drew Silva registered as latent. Causal review marked Eden Novak's chemical response dormant. Door and route checks placed Jules Meier's workshop room at waking. Witnesses in the corridor put Logan Kline's workshop room at clear. Reconstruction kept Yael Patel's treatment order at latent. A close photograph of the token set Drew Silva's tool stamp to latent. At final count, Eden Novak's tool stamp remained open.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 2

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. A witness who checked the roster left Drew Silva with a clear apprentice lineage. On the sealed worksheet, clerks wrote latent beside Eden Novak's apprentice lineage. Clocked entries put Jules Meier's work interval at latent. The sequence sheet showed Logan Kline's work interval as dormant. Downstream checks tied Yael Patel to a open chemical response. A movement sketch marked Drew Silva's workshop room as stable. The route ledger tied Eden Novak's workshop room to latent. In the ordered log, Jules Meier's treatment order appeared as open. The ordered sheet showed Logan Kline's treatment order as stable. Inventory counted Yael Patel's tool stamp as waking.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 3

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. In the earlier pairing note, Yael Patel carried a waking apprentice lineage. After the timesheet review, Drew Silva's work interval stayed stable. Reconciled timing notes kept Eden Novak's work interval at waking. Instruments tracing Jules Meier's action left the chemical response waking. When Logan Kline acted, the chemical response came back stable. Location review left Yael Patel's workshop room open. Sequence notes placed Drew Silva's treatment order at dormant. At sequence review, Eden Novak's treatment order stayed waking. Token and seal checks left Jules Meier's tool stamp at stable. The sealed check showed Logan Kline's tool stamp as clear.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 4

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. For this incident, the accepted tally was 13. The final definition was strict: the certified restoration lead was the one person whose six-stream tally equaled the accepted tally.
